title: Simplex attachment pushouts for a decomposition simplicial set
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and ordinary nerves from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and ordered joins from [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, $I$ a small ordinary category and $F:I\to\mathrm{sSet}_{/K}$ a functor, written $a\mapsto(\pi_a:K_a\to K)$. Let $K_F$ be the decomposition simplicial set defined by the two ordered blocks and compatible lifts in [lem-coef-decomposition-local-colimit-cocones]. For a face-stable family of subsets $L_r\subseteq K_r$ (meaning $d_j(L_r)\subseteq L_{r-1}$ for every face), define $L_F\subseteq K_F$ to be the simplicial subset generated by $N(I)$ and by all nondegenerate simplices of $K_F$ with nonempty lower block whose lower $r$-simplex belongs to $L_r$. Fix $m\geq0$ and $\sigma\in K_m\setminus L_m$, assume every proper face of $\sigma$ belongs to $L$, and let $L'$ agree with $L$ except that $L'_m=L_m\cup\{\sigma\}$.

Define $I_\sigma$ to have objects $(a,w)$ with $w\in(K_a)_m$ and $\pi_a(w)=\sigma$, and arrows $(a,w)\to(b,w')$ given by $u:a\to b$ with $F(u)(w)=w'$. Let $D_\sigma$ be the full subcategory on degenerate $w$, where degenerate means the pullback of a smaller-dimensional simplex by a noninjective surjective monotone map. Put $B=N(I_\sigma)$ and $B_0=N(D_\sigma)$. Define $c_\sigma:\Delta^m\star B\to K_F$ on a mixed simplex, consisting of $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$ and a chain $(a_0,w_0)\to\cdots\to(a_s,w_s)$, by lower block $\alpha^*\sigma$, upper chain $a_0\to\cdots\to a_s$, and lifts $\alpha^*w_j$. On the pure lower factor it is $\sigma:\Delta^m\to K$, and on the pure upper factor it is the forgetful map $B\to N(I)$. This is a simplicial map with image in $L'_F$.

If $\sigma$ is nondegenerate, $c_\sigma$ sends $\partial\Delta^m\star B$ into $L_F$ and the square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\partial\Delta^m\star B&\hookrightarrow&\Delta^m\star B\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow c_\sigma\\ L_F&\hookrightarrow&L'_F\end{array}$$
is a pushout in simplicial sets.

If $\sigma$ is degenerate, put
$$P_\sigma=(\partial\Delta^m\star B)\amalg_{\partial\Delta^m\star B_0}(\Delta^m\star B_0)\subseteq\Delta^m\star B.$$
Then $c_\sigma$ sends $P_\sigma$ into $L_F$ and the square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}P_\sigma&\hookrightarrow&\Delta^m\star B\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow c_\sigma\\ L_F&\hookrightarrow&L'_F\end{array}$$
is a pushout in simplicial sets. Here $\partial\Delta^m$ is the simplicial subset of $\Delta^m$ consisting of monotone maps with nonsurjective image; in particular $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$, and $X\star\varnothing=X$, so $\Delta^m\star B_0$ contains the pure lower factor even when $B_0$ is empty. Neither the maps $\pi_a$ nor $c_\sigma$ are required to be injective. No contractibility, weak homotopy equivalence, directedness or quasicategory assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Unpack the ordered-block definition of $K_F$. A simplex of a join is uniquely a lower monotone map followed by an upper nerve chain, and the compatibility equations for the lifts are preserved by precomposition, restriction to faces, and repetition. Therefore the displayed formula for $c_\sigma$ is simplicial; on the pure factors it is respectively $\sigma$ and the forgetful map to $N(I)$. Every image simplex has lower block a face or degeneracy of $\sigma$, hence belongs to $L'_F$ by the definition of the generated subset. The same check covers $m=0$ and empty upper or lower blocks.

source.place: HTT Notation 4.2.3.1, Remark 4.2.3.2 and the definition of the characteristic map in the proof of Proposition 4.2.3.8, printed pp. 248-252.

proof.text: Use the unique nondegenerate decomposition of each simplex of the simplicial set $K_F$. A simplex outside $L_F$ has a unique nondegenerate root whose lower block is outside $L$; after adjoining $\sigma$, the new roots are exactly those whose lower block is $\sigma$. Writing a root and all of its degeneracies in join coordinates gives a surjective monotone map $\alpha:[r]\twoheadrightarrow[m]$ and a chain of lift objects $(a_0,w_0)\to\cdots\to(a_s,w_s)$ in $I_\sigma$. Conversely these data determine the corresponding simplex of $K_F$. The nerve coordinates are therefore precisely the $B=N(I_\sigma)$ factor of $\Delta^m\star B$. If $\sigma$ is degenerate, the same decomposition shows that a new simplex with a degenerate first lift $w_0$ already has a lower nondegenerate root in a proper face of $\sigma$; exactly these coordinates form the subnerve $B_0=N(D_\sigma)$ and are old.

source.place: HTT Notation 4.2.3.7 and the first paragraph of the proof of Proposition 4.2.3.8, printed pp. 251-252; the unique-degeneracy bookkeeping is the Eilenberg-Zilber decomposition.

proof.text: Assume $\sigma$ is nondegenerate. By hypothesis every proper face of $\sigma$ lies in $L$, so a join simplex belongs to the old subset precisely when its lower monotone map is nonsurjective (a boundary simplex) or its upper block is pure. The preceding classification identifies all remaining simplices bijectively with the simplices of $\Delta^m\star B$ not in $\partial\Delta^m\star B$, and identifies their common old faces with $\partial\Delta^m\star B$. Thus the canonical map from the pushout of $\partial\Delta^m\star B\hookrightarrow\Delta^m\star B$ along $c_\sigma$ to $L'_F$ is degreewise bijective and commutes with all operators, hence is an isomorphism. This proves the stated pushout and also shows that no injectivity of any $\pi_a$ is used.

source.place: HTT proof of Proposition 4.2.3.8, nondegenerate simplex attachment square, printed p. 252.

proof.text:
Assume $\sigma$ is degenerate. The classification in Step 2 says that the old part of the join consists of the entire boundary join together with all join simplices whose lift chain lies in $B_0$; their intersection is $\partial\Delta^m\star B_0$. The pure lower factor is old as well, since the nondegenerate root of the degenerate simplex $\sigma$ has smaller dimension and is a proper face in $L$. Consequently the canonical map from
   $P_\sigma=(\partial\Delta^m\star B)\amalg_{\partial\Delta^m\star B_0}(\Delta^m\star B_0)$ into $L_F$ is well-defined, and the remaining simplices of $\Delta^m\star B$ map bijectively to $L'_F\setminus L_F$. Degreewise the resulting pushout map is therefore bijective; compatibility with operators follows from the block formula, proving the degenerate pushout square. This also covers $D_\sigma=\varnothing$, because $\Delta^m\star\varnothing$ still contains the pure lower factor.

source.place: HTT proof of Proposition 4.2.3.8, degenerate simplex attachment square, printed pp. 251-252.

proof.text: The boundary convention is the stated one: a simplex of $\Delta^m$ is in $\partial\Delta^m$ exactly when its monotone map has nonsurjective image, so $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. The preceding degreewise identifications are natural in faces and degeneracies and hence establish both squares as pushouts in simplicial sets, including all empty-factor cases.

split_report.summary: Split the HTT simplex-attachment statement by an explicit degreewise classification of new simplices in the decomposition simplicial set. The nondegenerate case is the boundary join pushout; in the degenerate case the old degenerate-lift subjoin is retained, giving the stated P_sigma pushout. No new child node was needed because the only imported non-elementary combinatorial input is the existing Mathlib unique nondegenerate decomposition leaf.

No arbitrary characteristic map, nonempty lift category, monomorphism of the structure maps or homotopy hypothesis is assumed.
